impact.affected_asset: Email address, device UUID, secret-key format and identifier fields, and authentication salt.
impact.attacker_capability: Receive an auth-start request at an attacker-controlled HTTPS host and use captured request values to request the reported salt from the corresponding 1Password server.
impact.security_effect: Leakage of authentication-related metadata to an external server and acquisition of a corresponding salt; the report describes weakened SRPx-key computation but not successful user-key computation when the master password and secret key remain secure.

causal_trace.summary: A sign-in server URL can designate an HTTPS endpoint outside 1Password control.

The reviewed validation accepts URL form/HTTPS rather than binding the destination to a trusted 1Password domain; the shown iOS routine rejects only a normalized string that cannot be parsed as a URL.
The clients submit POST /api/v3/auth/start requests to externally controlled hosts, carrying email, deviceUuid, skformat, and skid values.

An external endpoint receives authentication-related metadata; the reported values can be used in a request to obtain a salt, while the report states that secure master password and secret key still prevent successful computation of user keys.

failure.operation: Submission of POST /api/v3/auth/start to an externally controlled sign-in host

primary_invariant.statement: A sign-in request destination must be bound to a trusted 1Password service domain, rather than accepted solely because its URL is syntactically valid or HTTPS.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The reported configuration checked whether the URL preceded with HTTPS, and the shown iOS validation rejected only an unparsable normalized URL, permitting requests to servers outside 1Password control.

raw_refs.role: finding report and embedded code/request evidence

quality.review_notes: This is a report-grounded finding with embedded partial proprietary-code excerpts and captured request evidence. No public client patch, release-note detail, or regression-test artifact establishes the exact post-fix matching semantics; expected-negative behavior is derived from the report's trusted-domain recommendation and statement that later releases added validation.

remediation.invariant_restored: Accept sign-in URLs only when they belong to trusted 1Password domains, such as *.1password.com.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Android 7.9.4 and iOS 7.9.6 contain additional validation

target.component: Android and iOS sign-in server URL validation

oracle.expected_negative: A client with destination validation should reject a sign-in URL outside trusted 1Password domains and should not submit auth-start data to that host.
oracle.expected_positive: With a supplied external HTTPS sign-in URL in an affected client, an external server receives POST /api/v3/auth/start containing the reported authentication-related fields.
